slides.title: 5 prompts that write cold emails people **actually reply to**
slides.sub: Copy, paste, fill in the brackets. Save this for your next outreach day.

slides.title: The personal first line
slides.prompt: Read this about [prospect name]: [paste LinkedIn about / recent post]. Write 3 opening lines for a cold email that reference one specific detail. Max 20 words each. No flattery.
slides.tip: a real detail proves it isn't a mass email.

slides.title: The pain-point angle
slides.prompt: I sell [your offer] to [job title] at [type of company]. List the 5 most expensive problems they face weekly, ranked by how often they'd complain about it to a friend.
slides.tip: you pitch the problem they already feel, not your feature list.

slides.title: The 90-word email
slides.prompt: Write a cold email under 90 words to [prospect] about [problem]. Structure: 1 personal line, 1 problem line, 1 proof line ([result you got]), 1 low-effort question. No links.
slides.tip: short emails get read on a phone.

slides.title: The subject line test
slides.prompt: Give me 10 subject lines for this email: [paste email]. 2-5 words, lowercase, no punctuation tricks. Then pick the 3 most likely to be opened and say why.
slides.tip: boring-looking subjects look like a colleague wrote them.

slides.title: The no-reply follow-up
slides.prompt: Write a 2-sentence follow-up to this email: [paste email]. Add one new useful idea for [prospect's company]. Do not say 'just following up' or 'bumping this'.
slides.tip: a follow-up that adds value earns the reply.
